source_documents.title: Bright, Robust and Readily Accessible Fluorophore Family for NIR-II Bioimaging

reference_evidence_units.quote: DFT analysis reveals that the high extinction coefficients arise from enhanced oscillator strength and reduced fwhm, while the superior quantum yields result from low electron−phonon coupling strength and minimal nonradiative decays.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BM3
reference_evidence_units.statement: Brightness explained by a large S0-S1 oscillator strength and weak electron-phonon coupling.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Our calculations reveal that ECXb exhibits a significantly higher HR factor of 6.39 at 7.83 cm−1, approximately six times greater than that of BM3. This elevated HR factor in ECXb is primarily attributed to the rotational freedom of the xanthene bridge. In contrast, the incorporation of the oxygen-bridging atoms in BM3 effectively restricts this rotational motion, thereby reducing HR factors and nonradiative decay.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BM3 vs ECXb
reference_evidence_units.statement: Low-frequency Huang-Rhys factors are about six times smaller in BM3; the oxygen bridges restrict a rotation present in the benchmark dye.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Computed for the benchmark comparison only.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Both the enhanced oscillator strength f and the reduced fwhm contribute to the improved εmax of BM3.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BM3
reference_evidence_units.statement: Larger f and narrower band than ECXb.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This consistent Stokes shift indicates minimal structural reorganization between the ground and excited states, reflecting low reorganization energy and a relatively rigid molecular framework.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BM1-BM3
reference_evidence_units.statement: Stokes shift about 30 nm in all solvents.

reference_evidence_units.quote: BM3, however, presents a striking contrast: its large, rigid, planar structure drives pronounced Haggregation, severely compromising its solubility.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BM3
reference_evidence_units.statement: In PBS the absorption maximum moves from 896 to 733 nm (H-aggregate).

reference_evidence_units.quote: BM3, however, displays a markedly different behavior: severe aggregation in PBS drastically quenches its emission (Figures 3g and S5d). Strikingly, upon introducing Tween 80, the fluorescence intensity of BM3 in PBS surges nearly 10-fold, reaching brightness levels comparable to that in methanol.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BM3
reference_evidence_units.statement: Aggregation quenches emission; surfactant restores the monomer and about 10-fold intensity.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Furthermore, BM3, featuring cyclic amino groups as terminal substituents, demonstrates superior optical properties relative to BM1 and BM2, including red-shifted absorption/ emission and higher molar absorptivity and quantum yield, attributable to enhanced electron-donating capacity and conformational restraint.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BM3 vs BM1, BM2
reference_evidence_units.statement: The julolidine end groups give higher yield than dimethyl/diethyl amino analogues.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The small Huang-Rhys factors are traced to the oxygen bridges restricting a rotation that is free in the benchmark dye (computed comparison).

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: H-aggregation in PBS quenches emission; Tween 80 restores the monomer.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The paper explains the high brightness by a large oscillator strength and weak electron-phonon coupling (small Huang-Rhys factors, small Stokes shift) that keep nonradiative decay low.
